speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand these episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, can you describe exactly what happens just before an episode starts and how long they typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste you mentioned is a specific type of aura often associated with seizures originating in the temporal lobe. Do you have any history of head trauma, fever, or family members with similar neurological conditions?

speaker: Doctor
text: The post-ictal confusion and automatisms strongly suggest focal impaired awareness seizures. To confirm the diagnosis and localize the seizure focus, I need to see brain activity patterns. REQUEST TEST: EEG
